title: PID Control for Robotics
description: Master PID (Proportional-Integral-Derivative) control to create precise and stable robotic systems with micro-ROS.
objectives: Understand PID control theory and its components
Implement discrete PID controller on Pico W
Tune Kp, Ki, Kd gains experimentally
Apply PID for motor velocity control
Integrate PID with micro-ROS for remote control

materials.name: 10kΩ Potentiometers
materials.notes: For manual Kp, Ki, Kd adjustment

connections: Encoder A → GPIO 16 + 100nF Capacitor to GND
Encoder B → GPIO 17 + 100nF Capacitor to GND
L298N GND → Supply GND + Pico GND (common)
warnings: CRITICAL: Isolate motor supply from Pico (GND common only)
Capacitors on encoder reduce electrical noise
Encoder must be mechanically secure to motor shaft
Supply must provide adequate current (>1A for most motors)

theory.pid_basic: PID is closed-loop control algorithm. Calculates control signal based on three components: current error (P), accumulated past errors (I), rate of error change (D).
theory.proportional: Proportional term (Kp × error) responds to current error. High Kp = fast response but with overshoot. Alone, causes steady-state error.
theory.integral: Integral term (Ki × ∫error·dt) eliminates steady-state error by accumulating past errors. High Ki can cause overshoot and wind-up (integrator saturation).
theory.derivative: Derivative term (Kd × Δerror/Δt) predicts future behavior based on rate of change. Reduces overshoot but amplifies noise. Requires filtering.
theory.discrete_pid: In digital systems: P = Kp×e[k], I = Ki×Σe[k]×Δt, D = Kd×(e[k]-e[k-1])/Δt. Implement anti-windup (limit I) and low-pass filter on D.
theory.tuning: Tuning methods: Ziegler-Nichols (increase Kp until oscillation), manual (Kp→Ki→Kd), or automatic optimization. Start with Ki=Kd=0, adjust Kp, then add I and D.

steps.title: Assemble Complete System
steps.description: Build circuit with motor, encoder and display
details: Connect all components according to detailed diagram
Verify electrical isolation between motor supply and Pico
Configure OLED display to show values

steps.title: Add Integral Term (PI)
details: Implement anti-windup: limit integral between -100 and 100
Goal: eliminate residual error without excessive overshoot

steps.title: Add Derivative Term (PID)
details: Adjust Kd to reduce overshoot without making system slow

steps.title: Tuning Interface with Potentiometers
details: Read ADC0, ADC1, ADC2 from potentiometers
Display on OLED: setpoint, current velocity, error, Kp, Ki, Kd
Create graph on display showing velocity vs time
Test step response: change setpoint abruptly

steps.title: Integration with micro-ROS
details: Create publisher on /pid/state with: setpoint, velocity, error, Kp, Ki, Kd
Create /pid/tune service to adjust gains remotely
Use rqt_plot to visualize real-time response
Record experiments with ros2 bag for analysis

bipesProject.description: BIPES project with complete PID controller for DC motor. Includes anti-windup, derivative filter and OLED interface for real-time visualization.

solutions: Reduce Kp (proportional gain too high)
Reduce Ki (integrator wind-up)
Increase Kd if oscillation is high frequency
Check Δt (sampling time) is correct
Add dead zone on PWM (motor doesn't respond below ~30)
Implement rate limiter (limit maximum change per cycle)
Increase Ki (insufficient integral term)
Check anti-windup isn't too restrictive
Confirm no excessive static friction in motor
Verify PWM reaches correct value
Test with constant load applied to motor
Increase Kp (larger proportional response)
Reduce filter on derivative term (if α too low)
Check Δt isn't too large (reduce to 10-20ms)
Confirm motor doesn't have excessive load
Check adequate motor power supply
Implement more aggressive low-pass filter (α = 0.05)
Use moving average on derivative calculation (3-5 samples)
Add debounce capacitors on encoder (100nF)
Calculate derivative based on time-between-pulses, not pulses-per-time
Consider using PI only if D doesn't bring benefits
Implement clamping: limit integral_accumulated between fixed values
Use back-calculation: when PWM saturates, stop accumulating error
Implement conditional integration: only integrate if |error| < threshold
Reduce Ki if saturation occurs frequently
Zero integral when setpoint changes abruptly

challenges.title: Ziegler-Nichols Tuning
challenges.description: Apply classic method: set Ki=Kd=0, increase Kp until sustained oscillation (Kc), measure period (Pc), calculate gains: Kp=0.6×Kc, Ki=1.2×Kc/Pc, Kd=0.075×Kc×Pc. Compare with manual tuning.

challenges.title: Adaptive PID with Gain Scheduling
challenges.description: Implement multiple PID gain sets for different velocity ranges. Use aggressive gains at low velocity and conservative at high velocity. Automatic switching based on setpoint.

challenges.title: Cascade Control with Dual PID
challenges.description: Implement cascade control: outer PID controls angular position (slow, Δt=50ms), inner PID controls velocity (fast, Δt=10ms). Inner PID setpoint comes from outer PID output. Publish both loops to ROS2.
